PROPOSED RESOLUTION (ORCHESTRATOR DECISION REQUIRED, raised at the Phase 9 gate): thread ONE boolean through legalTools alongside the existing `repoConfigured` parameter (publishEnabled / noGit, derived by the impure caller from gitio.isRepo(root) — the same derivation core/freshness.ts:32's noGit already relies on, since Config has no noGit field and git.mode 'read-only' cannot distinguish the two modes). nextStageTool returns null for REVIEWED when publish is disabled, and the exported settled-for-report predicate counts a REVIEWED item as terminal in that mode ONLY. This is a signature change to a committed pure-core gate, not a closed-vocabulary widening; adding a `noGit` field to Config would be a §2.1 schema change and is NOT proposed.

GAP (the closing verify has no subject item): adapter/evidence.ts runVerify's second parameter is itemId and core/types.ts:945 makes itemId a REQUIRED field of every evidence record, but §3.2's closing verify judges the whole run. PROPOSED RESOLUTION: the closing verify passes the RUN id as the record's itemId and the report identifies it by kind 'verify' + a startedMs after the report call began + tree 'main'; scopePattern is '**' so every required scope runs (the §2.1 one-pattern limitation already recorded at tools.ts verifyScopePatternOf applies unchanged). This is a §2.6 SEMANTIC decision about one field, not a schema widening — flagged for the orchestrator because it changes what itemId means on run-level records.

assertions.text: handlePublish step 1 (branch check): a fixture that validates (verify record head H1), then moves HEAD by a branch switch WITHOUT touching any staged file's mtime — every mtime term still passes, the case mtimes cannot see — is DENIED with a message naming BOTH commits (record.head and current HEAD) before any staging, format or commit side effect: no commit is created, the index is unchanged, and the item stays REVIEWED

publish is serial in item order because the git index is a singleton (§4.2:1572, §4.3:1627), and handlePublish owns the index-safety half: with items A and B both REVIEWED in ONE tree, A's publish commits; B's publish — whose verify record head predates A's commit — is DENIED at step 1 naming both commits and creates NO commit, so exactly ONE new commit exists on the fixture after both calls. handlePublish neither computes nor reorders wave order (that is the 9.4c driver's, row 9.4c-publish-order); it never ships a green produced before the sibling commit existed

handlePublish step 2 stages fileScope ∪ testScope MINUS every path in run.startDirty: under git.preexistingDirty 'refuse' with a pre-existing dirty file inside the item's scope, publish DENIES, appends exactly one §2.11 question with origin 'scope-conflict' (read back via readQuestions), creates no commit, and leaves the dirty file byte-identical

the same fixture under git.preexistingDirty 'exclude': publish COMMITS without the user's WIP and records the skipped path for the report — the created commit's content, asserted via gitio.stagedNameStatus-equivalent name-status of that commit, CONTAINS the item's test file (the tests ARE the deliverable's proof and ship in the same commit) and does NOT contain the pre-existing dirty file, which is left byte-identical in the worktree

a CRASHING formatter (non-zero exit, spawn failure, or empty stdout on non-empty input) DENIES publish naming the formatter and the file, the file is byte-identical afterwards, and no commit is created — a crashed formatter's stdout is not a formatting verdict, and failure and dirty are distinct outcomes

handlePublish step 4 re-checks §2.6 freshness through core verifyFreshFor (BOTH conditions, never a hand-rolled mtime compare): on a FRESH verdict publish proceeds straight to the commit and runs NO re-verify at all — zero new verify records appended, no quarantine performed, no marker written. Freshness is consulted, not merely computed

a STALE freshness verdict triggers EXACTLY ONE auto re-verify, executed through evidence.runVerify (a §2.6 verify record is appended, start-stamped after the publish call began), and a PASSING re-verify lets publish proceed to the commit in the same call — publish neither loops nor re-checks freshness a second time

the auto re-verify's exclusions are the SAME derivation validate uses, not a re-implementation: the record's `excluded` list equals tools.ts foreignRedSet(store, runId, queue, itemId) computed on the same fixture — every OTHER queue item strictly below GREEN's testScope ∪ the §2.11 stale-red registry, with the publishing item's OWN test files never excluded (quarantining them would let the verify pass by not running the thing it proves)

a FAILING auto re-verify drops the item to GREEN with debugging set rather than looping: the item read back via store.loadItem shows state 'GREEN' and a non-null debugging annotation, publish returns a denial, NO commit is created, and no second verify is attempted in the same call — in the fixture the item's own test still passes, so it is the tree and not the item that is broken
